sources.finding: Uniform and Normalized are native two-component float fields and inherit the input image domain.
The CPU uses half-pixel centers. Normalized divides by per-axis display size; Uniform centers the coordinates, divides by the larger display axis and multiplies by two.

The GPU Uniform shader expresses the same ordered arithmetic as the CPU. Compiler reciprocal lowering can produce small Float32 rounding differences; the port records exact differences and bounded errors separately.
GPU Normalized divides the half-pixel coordinates by the display dimensions.
Native float2-to-float3 pads Z=0, and float2-to-color pads Z=0 and alpha=1. These are the only newly admitted width conversions; scalar means and integer casts remain excluded.
